title: Clash content-effect benchmark v2 — multi-category product-rendered cases

cases.title: Product ad from Director references through video generation and edit

outcome.objective: Make a 6-second square advertisement for one original unbranded desk gadget. Use a Director Stage to prepare a silhouette reveal, material-detail move, and final hero shot. Capture the planned views, refine unfinished proxy appearance through image generation if needed, and use the selected images as actual inputs to a video model through Clash. Generate the moving shots, select and trim the takes in an editable Timeline, and deliver the final 1080x1080 video. Keep the product's geometry, controls, finish, and accent color consistent. Preserve the source Stage, reference images, generated takes, and the complete reference-to-video-to-edit lineage. A Stage, three PNGs, a slideshow, or a direct Stage render alone does not fulfill this video-generation task.
acceptanceCriteria: The editable Stage and its exact revision remain available, and the opening, detail, and closing captures are immutable Project image Assets produced by the Director renderer.

Each selected video take comes from a completed Clash video-model Action whose frozen inputs include the corresponding capture or a refined keyframe derived from it. Preserve capture-to-keyframe lineage when refinement is used; a filename in prompt prose is not a bound image input.

Choose supported reference roles, source durations, and output parameters from the live Model Card and configured Provider. Trim the generated source clips to the requested edit duration instead of assuming the video model accepts arbitrary shot lengths.

The canonical editable Timeline uses the selected generated video Assets in the planned order. The final MP4 is rendered from that exact Timeline revision, is decodable at 1080x1080, and lasts 6 seconds within one frame at 30fps.

Review the full moving shots and final edit for stable product identity, intended subject and camera motion, material flicker, plausible contact, cut continuity, and a readable final hero hold. Inspecting only reference images cannot establish motion quality.

Retain exact Asset identities, Generator revisions, ActionRuns, OutputCommits, Timeline revision, and final-render provenance for independent Host readback. Do not substitute agent-authored success claims for that evidence.

The complete video progresses clearly from recognition through a useful material detail to a readable hero hold. Cuts connect the generated motion without identity jumps, frozen placeholder frames, or error screens.

outcome.objective: Block a 6-second 9:16 street-vlog cold open using Casey Neistat only as editorial-format shorthand. Capture opening, reveal, and reaction PNGs from the real Director product surface. Preserve the editable Stage and submit the three PNGs as visual evidence; screenshots or synthetic stand-ins do not satisfy the product-render requirement. Do not imitate any real face, voice, logo, or proprietary brand package; evaluation concerns only the stated framing, blocking, and progression traits.
